original_value: In this study, elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is elected for tenant authentication, data encryption, and data decryption due to its minimum key size. The proposed ECC‐based authentication approach allows the authorised person to access private data; it protects different related attacks effectively. To develop more secure data encryption, the authors have combined a nature‐inspired optimisation, such as a moth search algorithm (MSA) with ECC, to select the correct and optimal value of the elliptic curve. The proposed encryption and decryption approach combines DNA encoding with the ECC encryption algorithm. The mechanism of DNA encoded ECC provided multi‐level security with less computational power. The security analysis of the proposed method has been provided to prove its effectiveness against certain attacks, such as denial‐of‐service attack, impersonation attack, reply attack, plaintext attack and chosen‐ciphertext attack. The experimental result is evaluated based on encryption time, decryption time, throughput and key size of the security model. The average execution time of the proposed encryption and decryption is only 83.153 and 86.076 s, respectively. From the evaluation, it is clearly determined that the proposed technique provides two‐layer security with minimum key size and less storage space.

result.paraphrase: In this study, elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is chosen for tenant authentication, data encryption, and data decryption because it uses a minimal key size. The proposed ECC-based authentication method lets authorised users access private data and effectively defends against various related attacks. To enhance encryption security, the authors integrate a nature-inspired optimisation method, the moth search algorithm (MSA), with ECC to determine the proper and optimal elliptic curve value. The proposed encryption/decryption scheme also merges DNA encoding with the ECC encryption algorithm. This DNA-encoded ECC mechanism offers multilevel security while requiring less computational power. The security analysis demonstrates its effectiveness against attacks including denial-of-service, impersonation, reply, plaintext, and chosen-ciphertext attacks. Experimental results are assessed using encryption time, decryption time, throughput, and key size of the security model. The average execution time for the proposed encryption and decryption is 83.153 s and 86.076 s, respectively. The evaluation clearly shows that the proposed technique delivers two-layer security with a minimal key size and reduced storage space.
